text: #727, step 1 of #566's plan, recorded at #734's merge. Refines D-0301 and keeps D-0121, D-0305, D-0311, D-0314, D-0321, D-0352 and D-0359. invariant init drafts .invariant/repository.json from the checkout's regular files for a person to review, complete and commit on the base branch. It finds Go, Python and TypeScript parts, nested and mixed, without running repository code, commands or installers, following links, or entering dependency, generated or environment trees. A draft holds each part's directory, a maintained digest pin where the toolchain is known compatible, its dependency and check inputs, current-state documents, agent rules, deepest-directory ownership and explicit shared inputs. It supplies only commands it understands, under the existing Go, hash-locked pip and npm admission and the Go, pytest, Vitest and Jest selector rules, and a formatting check must fail on differences. Anything else stays an explicit unresolved requirement, never an invented not_applicable: unknown checks, missing or unsupported locks, incompatible toolchains, ambiguous ownership, no detected project, and test configuration the draft can't read, including pytest configuration a test command reaches below the part and pytest collection settings. An incomplete draft carries a top-level unresolved list that the unchanged loader refuses; a complete one loads. Init keeps an existing repository configuration even with -force, refuses linked destinations, writes nothing without a full Invariant commit pin, and says a gate that runs the configured checks is still needed. External intake stays disabled. The merger finished the build by hand after its review: two of three findings were real and are fixed with regression tests; the third, inherited Jest configuration, can't happen, because a part's own package.json ends Jest's configuration search.
